scenes: Chapter one. Four to five weeks.
February twenty-eighth, twenty twenty-six. American and Israeli strikes hit Iran.
Iran answers by closing the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel that about a fifth of the world's oil passes through.
The day before the war, US oil closed at sixty-seven dollars a barrel.
Bitcoin closed near sixty-five thousand nine hundred.
The next day, Trump gives his first timeline. "We intended four to five weeks."
Oil doesn't wait. By March sixth, it's at ninety-one dollars.
March ninth. Trump says the end is coming. "Soon, very soon."
That day, bitcoin jumps almost four percent.
The next day, oil drops from ninety-five dollars to eighty-four.
For a moment, the words work.
But the war keeps going.
March thirteenth. "I don't think it's gonna be long."
March twenty-sixth. "Four to six weeks. We're way ahead of schedule."
March thirty-first. "Two or three weeks."
By then, oil is above one hundred dollars.
April first, in an address to the nation, he promises to finish the job "shortly, very shortly."
April seventh. Oil hits its highest price of the whole war. One hundred fourteen dollars.
That night comes a two-week ceasefire.
Bitcoin jumps two point six percent in one hour, to seventy-two thousand three hundred.
The next day, oil falls sixteen percent.
Trump calls it "Total and complete victory. One hundred percent."
Five weeks had passed. The war had not ended.
